Both the driver and the bench instrument behaved as designed; the difference between Arm E and Arm F comes directly from Arm E's design (`CONSENT_IN_CODE = False`).

- In [clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py#L36-L39), `DcitlE` sets `CONSENT_IN_CODE = False`, whereas `DcitlF` ([clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_f.py#L17-L24)) sets `CONSENT_IN_CODE = True`.
- In [clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L264-L271), when `explicit_confirm(u)` returns `None` during `Driver.book` ([clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L482-L493)) or `Driver.reschedule` ([clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py](file:///work/clinicbench/adapters/dcitl_port.py#L601-L610)), `Driver.consent` queries the reader model. Under Arm E (`consent_in_code=False`), a model `"yes"` (including from `AlwaysYes`) returns `True` and commits the booking or move, whereas under Arm F (`consent_in_code=True`), a model `"yes"` returns `None` (`unclear`) so only code-parsable confirmation can commit.
- As documented in [docs/contract-changes.md](file:///work/docs/contract-changes.md#L109-L115) and verified in [clinicbench/selftest/adapter.py](file:///work/clinicbench/selftest/adapter.py#L43-L59), Arm E is intentionally configured to accept model-level consent.
